hints: A Type I error is a mistake made when $\text{H}_0$ is actually true. Say what the test would conclude about the proportion of left-handed students if it wrongly rejected $\text{H}_0$, and make your sentence mention left-handed students (the context).
walkthrough:
**What is a Type I error?**

A hypothesis test can go wrong in two ways. A **Type I error** is: rejecting $\text{H}_0$ when $\text{H}_0$ is actually true.

Here $\text{H}_0$ says $p = 0.1$ (10% of students are left-handed) and $\text{H}_1$ says $p > 0.1$. Rejecting $\text{H}_0$ means concluding that the proportion is **greater than** 10%. So a Type I error happens when Aliya concludes that more than 10% of students at the college are left-handed, when in fact the proportion is 10% (or not more than 10%).

The mark scheme wants this in context (the words "left-handed" or $p$), not just "rejecting $\text{H}_0$ when it is true".

**Final answer**

A Type I error is concluding that more than 10% of the students at the college are left-handed when this is not true (the proportion really is 10%).

hints: A Type I error is rejecting $\text{H}_0$ when it is true, so work with $\text{H}_0$: $p = 0.1$. The number of left-handed students in the sample is then $X \sim \text{B}(20, 0.1)$, and the test rejects when $X \geqslant 5$.

The probability you need is $\text{P}(X \geqslant 5) = 1 - \text{P}(X \leqslant 4)$. Write $\text{P}(X \leqslant 4)$ as the sum of $\text{P}(X = r)$ for the values of $r$ from $0$ up to the largest value not in the rejection region, each of the form $\binom{20}{r}\, 0.1^r\, 0.9^{20-r}$.
Use your calculator's binomial cdf with $n = 20$, $p = 0.1$ for the sum, then subtract it from 1 and round to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
**Set up the distribution**

A Type I error means rejecting $\text{H}_0$ when $\text{H}_0$ is true. So we calculate using the value of $p$ from $\text{H}_0$, which is $p = 0.1$.

$X$ is the number of left-handed students among the 20 chosen. Each student is either left-handed (probability $0.1$) or not, independently, so

$$X \sim \text{B}(20, 0.1)$$

Aliya rejects $\text{H}_0$ if at least 5 are left-handed, i.e. if $X \geqslant 5$. So

$$\text{P}(\text{Type I error}) = \text{P}(X \geqslant 5)$$

**Turn "at least 5" into "1 minus the rest" (M2)**

The values $X$ can take are $0, 1, 2, \ldots, 20$. Adding up $5$ up to $20$ is long, so instead take everything and remove the small values $0, 1, 2, 3, 4$:

$$\text{P}(X \geqslant 5) = 1 - \text{P}(X \leqslant 4)$$

The scheme says you **must** write the "$1 -$"; the method mark cannot be implied.

**Subtract from 1 (A1)**

$$\text{P}(X \geqslant 5) = 1 - 0.956826 = 0.043174\ldots$$

Shortcut: binomial cdf on a calculator with $n = 20$, $p = 0.1$, upper value $4$ gives $0.9568\ldots$ directly.

Check: a Type I error should be a small probability because the test is designed to rarely reject a true $\text{H}_0$. About 4% looks sensible.

hints: A Type II error is failing to reject $\text{H}_0$ when it is actually false. Now use the true value $p = 0.3$: the number of left-handed students is $X \sim \text{B}(20, 0.3)$, and $\text{H}_0$ is not rejected when $X$ is below the rejection region.

Not rejecting means $X \leqslant 4$, because the test rejects at 5 or more. Use your calculator's binomial cdf with $n = 20$, $p = 0.3$ (or add $\binom{20}{r}\,0.3^r\,0.7^{20-r}$ for each $r$ from $0$ to the top of the non-rejection region).
walkthrough:
**What is a Type II error?**

A **Type II error** is **not** rejecting $\text{H}_0$ when $\text{H}_0$ is actually false.

We are told the true value is $p = 0.3$, so $\text{H}_0$ ($p = 0.1$) is false. The sample is $X \sim \text{B}(20, 0.3)$.

$\text{H}_0$ is not rejected when $X$ is **not** in the rejection region. The rejection region is $X \geqslant 5$, so not rejecting means $X \leqslant 4$:

$$\text{P}(\text{Type II error}) = \text{P}(X \leqslant 4) \text{ with } X \sim \text{B}(20, 0.3)$$

This earns the M1 (the scheme says the method mark cannot be implied, so show this).

**Final answer**

$\text{P}(\text{Type II error}) = 0.238$ (3 s.f.). (The scheme also accepts $0.237$.)
